input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Dashboard run comparison view for training and pipeline runs

## Description

Delivers the run comparison capability in the Dashboard: users select two or
more training or pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics side by
side, including a diff presentation that highlights which parameters and
metrics changed between two selected runs. This replaces the current
spreadsheet-export workflow for comparing candidate runs during model
promotion decisions.

## Scope

- Multi-select of runs from the Dashboard runs list (both training runs and
  pipeline runs).
- Side-by-side view of parameters and metrics for the selected runs.
- Diff presentation mode for a comparison of exactly two runs, highlighting
  the parameters and metrics whose values differ.
- The comparison reads run parameters and metrics from the run data the
  Dashboard already surfaces; Data Science Pipelines requires no code changes
  for this and is validated through the acceptance criteria below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given two or more runs selected from the runs list, When the user opens the
  comparison, Then the parameters and metrics of every selected run are
  displayed side by side in a single Dashboard view.
- Given exactly two runs in the comparison, When the diff presentation is
  enabled, Then parameters and metrics whose values differ between the two
  runs are highlighted and distinguishable from unchanged ones.
- Given both pipeline runs and training runs exist in a project, When runs of
  either kind are selected for comparison, Then the same comparison surface
  renders their parameters and metrics correctly (passive validation of Data
  Science Pipelines — no changes to that component).
- Given a selected run with no recorded parameters or metrics, When it is
  compared, Then the comparison renders without errors and marks the missing
  values.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and
  metrics side by side in the Dashboard.
- HLR-3 (P1): a run diff view highlighting which parameters and metrics
  changed between two selected runs. HLR-3 is a presentation mode of the same
  comparison surface over the same run data as HLR-1, so both requirements are
  covered by this epic at the higher priority (P0).

# Run lineage on registered model versions

## Description

Establishes, in the Model Registry, a resolvable link from a registered model
version back to the run (training or pipeline) that produced it, so that
platform surfaces can resolve and compare the run behind a registered model.
This is the registry-side foundation for opening a run comparison from the
Model Registry.

## Scope

- Represent the producing run on registered model versions, using the existing
  custom-properties extension point on ModelVersion entities as the
  architecture-defined mechanism for attaching structured metadata.
- Expose the lineage through the Model Registry REST API so the Dashboard can
  resolve the run behind a model version.
- Define behavior for model versions registered without run linkage: the
  absent lineage must not break registry operations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a run, When the version is retrieved
  through the Model Registry REST API, Then it carries a resolvable reference
  to the run that produced it.
- Given a model version with no producing run recorded, When the version is
  retrieved, Then the missing lineage is represented cleanly and registry
  operations continue to work.
- Given the lineage reference is read by a consumer, Then it is sufficient to
  identify the run in the Dashboard (project and run identity).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them (registry backend portion of the requirement).

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry

## Description

Adds the Dashboard entry point that opens the run comparison for the run
linked to a registered model version, completing the registry-to-comparison
workflow: a user reviewing registered models can jump straight to the
side-by-side and diff comparison of the run that produced a candidate model
version.

## Scope

- In the Dashboard's Model Registry view, surface an action on a model version
  that opens the run comparison populated with the run recorded in the
  version's lineage.
- Reuse the Dashboard run comparison capability (side-by-side parameters and
  metrics view and diff presentation) as the destination of the navigation.
- Handle model versions whose lineage is absent: the entry point is hidden or
  disabled without errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version that carries run lineage, When the user
  opens that version in the Dashboard's Model Registry view, Then an entry
  point is available that opens the run comparison populated with the linked
  run.
- Given a model version without run lineage, When its view is opened, Then no
  broken entry point is rendered and no error occurs.
- Given the linked run is opened for comparison, Then the same side-by-side
  and diff presentations are available as when comparing from the runs list.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry (Dashboard
  UI portion of the requirement).

# Documentation for the run comparison workflow

## Description

Documents the run comparison workflow end to end for data scientists: how to
compare runs from the runs list (side-by-side parameters and metrics plus the
diff presentation) and how to open a comparison from the Model Registry via a
model version's run lineage.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Comparing runs from the runs list: selecting two or more training or
  pipeline runs, reading the side-by-side parameters and metrics view, and
  using the diff presentation to see what changed between two runs.
- Opening a comparison from the Model Registry: navigating from a registered
  model version to the comparison of the run that produced it.
- Coverage of both run kinds (training runs and pipeline runs) in the
  walkthroughs.
- Placement of the new topics within the existing Dashboard and Model Registry
  documentation sets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation includes a complete walkthrough of comparing runs from the
  runs list, covering run selection, the side-by-side view, and the diff
  presentation.
- Documentation includes a complete walkthrough of opening a comparison from
  the Model Registry through a model version's run lineage.
- Documentation covers both training runs and pipeline runs.
- Content is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior before
  publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs
  list and the registry.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9015: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs

Triage: full decomposition (not below-threshold — the strategy spans three
components and multiple teams, and mixes Dashboard/Model Registry code
implementation with substantive documentation authoring; not docs-only — code
changes are required in Dashboard and Model Registry).

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E001 | Dashboard run comparison view for training and pipeline runs | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E002 | Run lineage on registered model versions | Implementation | Model Registry | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E003 | Open run comparison from the Model Registry | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E004 | Documentation for the run comparison workflow | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 Dashboard run comparison view (P0)"] --> E003["E003 Open comparison from Model Registry (P1)"]
    E002["E002 Run lineage on model versions (P1)"] --> E003
    E001 --> E004["E004 Comparison workflow docs (P1)"]
    E002 --> E004
    E003 --> E004
```

E001 and E002 are roots and run in parallel (different components, different
repos, no shared artifacts). Critical path length: 3 (E001 → E003 → E004, or
E002 → E003 → E004).

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E003 | Rule 13 (build-against artifact) | The registry entry point navigates into the run comparison view; the consuming Dashboard work builds against the comparison surface produced by the comparison epic. |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 13 (build-against artifact) | The registry entry point resolves the producing run through the Model Registry REST API lineage surface; it is an API the consumer builds against, not a configuration reference. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation describes the implemented comparison workflow. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation describes the registry-side lineage workflow. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation describes opening a comparison from the registry. |
| (no edge) E001 ∥ E002 | Rule 14 (parallel) | Different components and repos with no shared artifacts; the P0 comparison work must not be gated by the P1 registry lineage work. |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) |
|-----|----------|---------|
| HLR-1 — select two or more runs, view parameters and metrics side by side | P0 | E001 |
| HLR-2 — registered model versions link back to the producing run; comparison openable from the Model Registry | P1 | E002 (registry backend), E003 (Dashboard entry point) |
| HLR-3 — run diff view highlighting changed parameters and metrics | P1 | E001 (consolidated with HLR-1) |
| HLR-4 — documentation covers the comparison workflow | P2 | E004 |

All HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

**HLR consolidation note (HLR-1 + HLR-3):** HLR-3's diff view is a
presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run data as
HLR-1 — the strategy itself notes the requirements were consolidated from two
customer councils with overlapping wording kept. Per the redundant-HLR rule
they are ONE capability covered by a single epic (E001) at the higher priority
(P0). Splitting them would produce two epics building the same surface plus an
artificial serialization edge.

**Priority note on E004:** HLR-4 is P2 in the strategy, but the
docs-authoring priority exception derives the docs epic's priority from the
strategy frontmatter (`priority: Major` → P1). The exception also means E004
does not push P1 upstream to the implementations it depends on.

## Component Mapping Notes

- All epic `component` values are copied verbatim from
  `.context/rhai-components.txt`: `Dashboard`, `Model Registry`,
  `Documentation`.
- **Data Science Pipelines is passive.** It is listed as affected but needs no
  code changes — run parameters and metrics are already exposed through the
  existing per-run surfaces the Dashboard reads. Validation (comparison
  renders parameters and metrics correctly for pipeline runs and training
  runs) is an acceptance criterion on E001, the nearest active component's
  epic, validated by the same (Dashboard) team — no separate validation epic
  is warranted.
- HLR-2 spans two components: the lineage representation on model versions
  (Model Registry backend, E002) and the user-facing entry point (the
  registry UI lives in the Dashboard per architecture context, E003). This is
  an architectural split along component/team boundaries, not a priority
  split.
- Teams were derived from the architecture-context owning-team fields
  (`RHOAI Dashboard`, `Model Registry`) because the strategy lists no teams.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections** (non-blocking): Affected Components is a bare
  list with no change descriptions or owner teams; there is no Impacted Teams
  table, no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no
  non-functional requirements. Epic acceptance criteria were derived from the
  HLRs; teams were derived from architecture context.
- **Docs epic ownership assumption:** the strategy names no documentation
  owner. E004 is assigned to the RHOAI Dashboard team as owner of the primary
  documented surface; confirm the owner before implementation.
- **"Training runs" source unspecified:** the title and problem statement
  reference training runs, but Training Operator is not among the affected
  components. E001 treats run kinds as whatever the Dashboard's existing run
  surfaces expose and carries an AC covering both pipeline and training runs;
  if training-run metadata turns out to be inaccessible, that is a fix-and-
  retry implementation matter (no open question in the strategy suggests a
  different epic structure).
- **Priority observation:** HLR-4 is P2 in the strategy while the docs epic
  carries P1 — this is the docs-authoring priority exception (Major → P1), not
  an inversion.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependencies with uncertain timing; all work is
in-platform.
